escalation.obstacle: Decide whether any of the 491 surviving non-adjacent pairs is forced equal at k=5, i.e. c(p)=c(q) in every 5-colouring of the 553-vertex point set. If one is, it is a genuine forced-equal DISTINCT pair and, per the geometry branch's current direction, gives them a finite amplifier; its exact d^2 is what they need.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. A pair is forced equal at k if G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not; the added edge is a combinatorial disequality constraint, not a unit edge, because |p-q| != 1. Coordinates live in Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11) with basis [1,3,5,11,15,33,55,165].
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; complete finite graph; k = 5; no measurability, periodicity or lattice hypothesis.
